action_proposals.description: The previous rollouts failed primarily due to the white carton toppling over. This was caused by pushing from too high a contact point (Rollouts 1 & 3) or pushing too aggressively in a single motion (Rollout 2). Rollout 4 was the most successful because it addressed the toppling issue by first descending to a lower contact point and then breaking the push into two segments. However, it failed to push the carton far enough, leaving a 3.5 cm gap. This optimized plan builds directly on the successful strategy of Rollout 4. It incorporates the same descent to a low contact point to prevent toppling. It also uses a multi-stage push for better control. The total push distance is increased by more than 3.5 cm to correct the final alignment error observed in the last rollout.

action_sequence.reasoning: Approach the white carton, aligning the gripper with its center before descending.
Descend to a low contact point on the carton. This was the key strategy from the most successful rollout to prevent tipping.
Perform the first part of a segmented push. This applies force gradually to maintain stability.
Continue with the second part of the segmented push to move the carton most of the required distance.
Perform the final push to cover the remaining distance and correct the 3.5 cm alignment error from the last rollout.
Lift the gripper to retract cleanly away from the carton after the push is complete.
